dedupe_keys.name: dft transport connectivity metric england and wales 2025

description: The transport connectivity metric, published by the UK Department for Transport on 29 September 2025, measures how well people in England and Wales can reach jobs, services and social destinations by walking, cycling, driving and public transport. Coverage and contents: one-hour connectivity scores for 2021 output areas and lower super output areas, also summarised by local authority district and region, built from population-weighted origins, destinations weighted by value (schools and colleges, healthcare from pharmacies and GPs to hospitals and emergency departments, shopping, leisure and community sites, workplaces) and people's willingness to travel. Destination data come from Department for Education records, NHS England, Ordnance Survey AddressBase and Greenspaces, OpenStreetMap and the Business Register and Employment Survey. Format and access: ODS tables with metadata on GOV.UK; estimates for about 15 million 100 m squares feed a Connectivity Tool open only to local authorities and government. Licence and cost: free under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Caveats: first estimates; it measures opportunity to travel, not trips, and has no assignment. The scores give baseline access to critical facilities by mode, which network and resilience models can compare after a transit or road disruption. It relates to the DfT Journey Time Statistics in the catalogue.
